chapter: Porch interview and Jazz Train plans
title: Fats Waller biographies omit Johnson; 'The Joint Is Jumpin''
summary: Rasch complains biographies of Fats ignore Johnson, mentions 'Ain't Misbehavin'' and a college performance of 'The Joint Is Jumpin''.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: One of the things that is very important with Tom -- I told him -- I read a couple of biographies about Fats Waller. I mentioned this to you once before, J.C. They don't do justice to you. One of them doesn't mention J.C. at all, and he had a very strong influence on Fats. In fact, at his funeral, (inaudible) J.C. to be chief pall-bearer because that's how Fats would have wanted it. And a lot of people, they hear the name Johnson and they say, oh, that's J.C. Johnson. So they give J.C. credit. And this is one of the things that's my heart's desire, to straighten that record out.
That's one of the things that -- that's why the Smithsonian is now on my tail to get the thing finished. But I tell them that there are things that only you can make accurate.
Fats Waller was a piano player, was he a singer?
(Inaudible) wonderful musician.
He was an older man than you?
I wouldn't say that (inaudible).
You were older than he was.
Sure, I (inaudible) older than he was. Yeah, sure was.
Did you write some stuff that he performed or how did your friendship get going?
We were youngsters, growing together during that era. We were around together.
You were about the same age. See, I couldn't --
I was a little older than him.
A couple of years, maybe.
But -- yeah.
Oh, I couldn't figure whether (inaudible).
No, he was (inaudible).

Now, in Ain't Misbehavin', which is a musical about Fats Waller's life, except it doesn't do justice to him, as J.C. says, (inaudible) really about him, but three of the songs in there are songs that J.C. collaborated with him on, including -- I don't think you watch television. He doesn't watch television.
(Inaudible.)
No. But The Joint's Jumpin' is an incredible song, and J.C. did the words for it, Fats did the music for it. And we had Jim Chapin, Harry Chapin's father,

doing a jazz performance at the college. And we asked him if he would play one of the songs, and I gave him a whole list and that was the only one I could dig out. And he played that song. And that one was the hit of the whole night. Everything else fell by the wayside. And that was even without a lot of rehearsal time on it. He got the information at the last minute.
(Inaudible.)
That's what J.C. does.
